reachable: Yes, at the scored position and with gradient in training. (1) The target is a global linear map applied unconditionally: make_target returns z @ F.t() at every training cmd position, and eval/adapter.py:197-198 deep-copies the TRAINED net.target_module and hands it to the probe, where evolve/cups_probe.py:275 calls to_obs(pred, z_prev) on the read prediction. Nothing about either map is gated on an observation being present, and to_obs ignores z_prev entirely (verified: identical output for zeros vs random z_prev). (2) The delta statistics actually accumulate in the real loop — I ran H._train with the exact genome.json on 400 real sequences for 25 steps: ok=True, _n_observed=25, _n_delta=25, delta_moment moved off I by 1.14; over 400 real batches _n_delta=400/400 and the map rebuilds (first rebuild at step 200, then every 100). The rebuild gates (min_rows=32, warmup=200 on both counters) are comfortably met at bs=64 x ~30 cmd steps = ~1920 rows/step. (3) The crossed-in head is live at the scored read: gates come from the command embedding alone, the read at slot i is taken strictly before slot i's write, and rho collapses to 0 when the observation slot is padded — so the read still contributes through the zero-init out_scale, which does receive gradient (0.0076 after 25 real steps). (4) r22_prefix_content_xattention inherits R18PathStateLatentTransition, which defines transition_from_emb, so the head's fm term is live (fm_off=False) as the hypothesis claims. (5) The target module has no parameters, only buffers, so nothing in it is trained — but nothing in it needs to be; the loss geometry it defines is what the arch's parameters chase.
solves_outside_model: Clean. The new code parses no command, resolves no chain, and touches nothing but the target tensors: F and Finv are one global 768x768 matrix built from two second-order statistics of the TRAINING split's embeddings (an EMA second moment of targets, and an EMA of unit-normalized lower-half consecutive-difference outer products), rebuilt on CPU in float64 and applied identically at every step, every window, every candidate and both arms of the role swap. z_prev enters only inside _observe_delta under `self.training and torch.is_grad_enabled()` — verified frozen in eval mode and under no_grad — and is not an argument of either map, so the delta-target gating hazard the hypothesis says it avoids is genuinely avoided. Because the map is a fixed invertible linear operator applied to both arms identically, it cannot by itself create a native-vs-swapped difference; it can only change the training geometry. The retrieval comparison still happens in the fixed observation space through an exact inverse (inv@fwd - I max abs 1.5e-7, public round-trip error 4.8e-6, both at float32 buffer precision, same as the parent's). No statistic is taken from the scored split. The prior-retraction shape (resolved routing stamped into the input) has no analogue here.
summary: The code implements the mechanism it describes, and the parts of the description that are checkable by execution check out — including the ones the author could not have measured but stated anyway, which turn out to be right. Verified by execution: Finv F = I by construction (1.5e-7); the trace renormalization does hold tr(F S_shrunk F^T) = dim (95.99999996 at dim=96); the local-change moment is carried into the FULLY whitened frame (mu^-1/2) as claimed even though the whitening exponent is p=0.75; S_d keeps trace = dim; and — the strongest single check — setting disc_power=0 reproduces the parent zca_shrunk_target_whitening's forward AND inverse maps BIT-EXACTLY (max|diff| = 0.0 for both), so "a strict extension of the mechanism it is crossed with" is literally true, normalizing constant included. The two numbers the hypothesis reports from the jail sample are accurate: exactly-zero consecutive pairs 20.4% in evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl and 18.1% on the full encoded pack ("about a fifth"), same-shape neighbours 31.0% / 33.6% ("about a third"). The author's own flagged untested assumption — risk #2, that the lower-half magnitude cut might select format switches rather than same-context content differences — does NOT materialize on real embeddings: median d2 is 774 for content-content pairs versus 1500-2100 for every cross-format class, and the kept band is 2.4x enriched in content-content pairs (26.7% of kept vs 10.9% of population) while listing-listing is depleted (13.8% vs 22.7%). The resulting map amplifies same-board content directions more than format-switch directions. The cost estimate is also accurate (0.102s per rebuild vs the parent's 0.045s at half the frequency: 4.1s vs 3.6s of CPU rebuild per 4000 steps). What does not survive is the "second, compounding effect" paragraph: the content-differing pairs it says are at risk of being masked as duplicates by r12 sit 20x above the duplicate threshold in raw space already, and the candidate's map moves their hard-negative ring weight 3x BELOW the parent's rather than raising it. That is a falsified prediction about an inherited component, not a code-vs-spec mismatch, but it is asserted in the text that will be archived as this candidate's description. Separately, the delivered gain differential over the parent is only ~8% (gains 0.33-1.73, median 1.035, no clipping at the cap), which sits close to the author's own "benign failure" branch and, against a 0.0227 noise floor, means a three-seed draw may not separate this from its parent either way.

divergences.claim: "Stretching exactly the content-difference subspace pushes those pairs out of the duplicate band and into the ring... the same matrix that fixes the geometry of the regression also re-aims the contrastive term at the eval's own decision" — i.e. under raw/whitened metrics, observations differing only in a content hash risk being masked out as duplicates by r12's dupmask, and the new map rescues them into the hard-negative ring.
divergences.what_the_code_does: Both halves are wrong, and the second is reversed. r12 computes tt = per-dimension mean squared target-target distance and dupmask = 1 - exp(-tt/0.05). On 4014 real same-board, content-token-only-differing observation pairs the raw per-dim tt is median 1.013 (q05 0.680) — 20x above _DELTA=0.05 — so dupmask = 1.0000 for every one of them before any whitening. They were never in the duplicate band. Meanwhile the ring weight (confus*dupmask, with lam = 0.5*mean_off) for exactly those pairs FALLS as the map stretches them: 0.367 raw -> 0.092 under the parent's whitening -> 0.028 under the candidate's map, because pushing them past 0.5*mean_off moves them out of the confusability window. The candidate gives the eval's own discriminating pairs ~3x LESS hard-negative boost than the parent, not more.

divergences.claim: "discards rows whose d is (numerically) exactly zero"
divergences.what_the_code_does: _observe_delta drops rows by a relative threshold, pos = live & (d2 > 1e-4 * mean(d2 over live rows)), not by an exact-zero test. On real data the two sets coincide exactly, so there is no behavioural difference on this pack; on a pack whose mutation observations were near-constant rather than byte-identical the epsilon would drop strictly more than the text describes.

divergences.what_the_code_does: Near-identical targets get ~0 ring BOOST (a_raw = 1 + kappa*ring collapses to 1), not zero weight; they remain ordinary in-batch negatives in the softmax denominator, merely relatively downweighted after the row-mean normalization of `a`. The phrasing is copied from the objective impl's own DESCRIPTION, so it is inherited rather than invented.

divergences.claim: "the parent additionally ran with pred_weight = 0.0, so only its memory read was supervised"
divergences.what_the_code_does: pred_weight gates one extra NCE term on the arch's prediction INSIDE the head's aux loss; with 0.0 only the head's memory-read terms remain in the aux. The arch's prediction is of course still supervised by the main objective. Loose phrasing, correct in context.
